voicevox.credit: VOICEVOX:<character> (for example VOICEVOX:ずんだもん), placed where viewers can find it (description or credits)

ずんだもん terms: credit 'VOICEVOX:ずんだもん'; no political or religious use, no information products, no deliberately misleading content; credit-free commercial use is a paid contract

the terms of the other characters were not checked (unverified): refused unless the caller acknowledges it (--accept-unverified-voice-terms); the credit is then derived as 'VOICEVOX:<name>' and marked unverified (ADR-006)
--voice is a VOICEVOX style id (the API's `speaker`); default 3, ずんだもん ノーマル
voicevox.weights_license: per voice library terms (not an OSS licence); commercial use allowed with credit for the ずんだもん / 四国めたん voices; other characters unverified (refused unless acknowledged, ADR-006)

execution.engine_process: worker subprocess in its own process group (under the engine's own interpreter when configured), killed on --timeout; Hugging Face libraries forced offline
execution.offline_flag: accepted everywhere; every registered engine works with no network (loopback only)
execution.overwrites: never unless --overwrite; an output equal to an input is refused

cue.speaker: optional speaker id (diarization-skill), mapped to a voice
cue.text: the line to speak, already in `lang`

cues.format: JSON list of cues, or an SRT / WebVTT file (subtitle-skill output)
cues.lang: BCP-47 language of the text (ja, en, ...); must be one of the engine's languages
cues.translation: done by the caller before this skill is called; optionally described with --translation-note (engine, reviewer) so it is recorded in the provenance. No engine is chosen here

translation.detail: this skill does not translate: the caller passes cues whose text is already in the target language (ADR-003). The machine-translation engine is an open decision owned by subtitle-skill.

not_provided: translation / machine translation of the script (caller input, ADR-003; subtitle-skill owns 字幕翻訳)
noise reduction, voice isolation of the source (voice-enhance-skill, audio-production-skill)
final mix and loudness targets of the programme (audio-production-skill)
downloading engines or model weights (one-time manual step; doctor says how)
network access beyond loopback (VOICEVOX / Style-Bert-VITS2 run on this machine)
direct ffmpeg calls (every media step is an ffmpeg-skill tool)

consent_record.checked: in the op before any engine work (the record first, then the clip's hash), and again in the worker
consent_record.error: CONSENT_REQUIRED (exit 2): details.reason is no_record | record_not_found | record_invalid | reference_mismatch, details.problems lists every problem

fields.evidence: [{path (relative to the record), sha256}]: at least one file (signed form, recording of the consent); every file must exist and match
fields.expires_at: optional; past it the record does not count
fields.granted_at: ISO 8601 date-time with a UTC offset; not in the future
fields.reference.sha256: the SHA-256 of the reference clip the consent covers
fields.voice_owner.name: the person whose voice it is

policy.credit: an engine's credit (credit_required) is carried into the provenance and must appear in the published video's description or credits; VOICEVOX credits are resolved per voice ('VOICEVOX:<character>', with the speaker and the character) into each clip's provenance `credits` and the op's `obligations`
policy.voice_cloning: a reference voice (or a model trained on a real person's voice) is used only with a consent record of that person that checks out (CONSENT_RECORD, ADR-009): the op verifies it before any engine work, and the engine verifies it again in the worker; otherwise CONSENT_REQUIRED. There is no flag, option or environment variable that skips the gate

voicevox.unverified: refused with TERMS_UNVERIFIED unless the caller passes --accept-unverified-voice-terms; the credit is then derived as 'VOICEVOX:<name>' and recorded with terms_verified: false

conditions: commercial and non-commercial use allowed with the credit
no political or religious use, no information products, no deliberately misleading content
credit-free commercial use needs a paid contract
commercial and non-commercial use allowed with the credit
no political or religious use, no information products, no deliberately misleading content
credit-free commercial use needs a paid contract

policy.watermark: an engine's watermark is never removed or bypassed; it is recorded in the provenance, and Chatterbox's Perth mark is read back from every clip (a clip where it is not found is refused)

tools.description: Narration from text or cues: one clip per line by a local engine (worker subprocess), laid on one mono timeline WAV through ffmpeg-skill (pad + join), validated through ffmpeg-skill/probe
inputs: cues (CUES_INPUT: .json, .srt, .vtt) or plain text (.txt, one utterance per line, back to back)
the engine's built-in voice (voicevox: a style id, default 3), or a reference voice (--reference, chatterbox) with its owner's consent record (--consent, CONSENT_RECORD, ADR-009)
tools.output: mono PCM WAV at the first clip's sample rate (Chatterbox: 24 kHz; VOICEVOX: the outputSamplingRate of its audio_query, 24 kHz by default); one clip per line, each placed at its cue start (cues) or back to back (text); the timeline lasts to the later of the last clip and the last cue end

refused.timed cues: FFMPEG_SKILL_UNAVAILABLE while ffmpeg-skill/pad cannot take audio-only input (ADR-005)

tools.description: Dialogue replaced with translated speech (ADR-008): one clip per translated cue by a local engine, fitted to its source segment (timing fit, ADR-007, tempo 1.0), spoken over the programme's own audio lowered by --duck dB while the line is spoken, and put back into the video; every media step through ffmpeg-skill (audio, cut, join, probe)
inputs: the programme: a video (or an audio file with a .wav output)
translated cues (CUES_INPUT), one per source segment at its times; translation is the caller's (ADR-003)
optional source cues (--source-cues): checked to be the same segments, the source text hash recorded

a voice per cue speaker (--speaker-voice SPEAKER=VOICE, else --voice), or a reference voice per speaker (--speaker-reference SPEAKER=PATH, else --reference) with its owner's consent record (--speaker-consent / --consent, CONSENT_RECORD, ADR-009)

max_overrun.bounded_by: the next cue's start and the programme's end

tools.output: the programme with its audio replaced (video stream-copied), or the new programme audio as PCM WAV; as long as the programme, audio as long as the picture (max(0.1 s, 1 %))

refused.a line longer than its room: TIMING_OVERFLOW unless --on-unfit keep (the original dialogue stays there)
refused.plain text: INVALID_ARGUMENT: each line replaces the dialogue of its segment, so cues are needed

render.silence: none is made: the time between lines is the programme's own sound
render.tempo: ffmpeg-skill has no audio-only tempo change (fit and speedramp declare audio_only: false), so DUB speaks every line at tempo 1.0; a line longer than its room is unfit (ADR-007, ADR-008)

tools.description: Audio description (ADR-010): description cues spoken only inside the programme's gaps (the caller's, or its quiet stretches found by ffmpeg-skill/silence), each from its cue's start and ending by its cue's end and its gap's end, over the programme's own sound lowered by --duck dB; the renderer is DUB's
inputs: the programme: a video (or an audio file with a .wav output)
the engine's voice (voicevox: a style id), or a reference voice with its owner's consent record (ADR-009)
tools.output: the programme with its audio replaced (video stream-copied), or the new programme audio as PCM WAV; every placed description inside its gap; as long as the programme, audio as long as the picture

tools.description: Timing fit (ADR-007): one clip per cue measured through ffmpeg-skill/probe against its cue window; per line fit (tempo 1.0, silence after), tempo (the smallest speed-up within --max-tempo) or unfit (reported with the reason, the tempo it would need and the seconds over; never cut, never placed); the silence before each placed line and after the last. Writes no media
inputs: one audio clip per cue, in cue order
tools.render: ffmpeg-skill has no audio-only tempo change (fit and speedramp use atempo but declare audio_only: false and refuse an input without video) and no audio-only pad, so the plan is not rendered; DUB (step 5) and NARRATE render it once ffmpeg-skill can (ADR-007)

statuses.unfit: over_limit | empty_slot | empty_clip | not_measured: reported, TIMING_OVERFLOW unless --on-unfit report

tools.description: What is installed and missing (engines, ffmpeg-skill) and how to get it; never downloads
Registered engines with status, version, licences, credit and watermark
